subject.title: Feature Request: Cross-platform migration tool (migrate export/import)

question: Should OpenClaw own automated same-product archive import/restore for cross-platform migration, and if so should that surface live under `migrate`, `backup`, or a narrower preview/convert/manual-restore flow?
rationale: Automation cannot safely choose the product and security boundary because the request crosses destructive local state writes, credentials, session history, workspace files, path remapping, and an existing provider-based `migrate` namespace.

options.title: Design Minimal Core Migration Contract
options.body: Define a preview-first first-party export/import or backup-restore contract with safe extraction, explicit secret/session policy, path remapping, conflict handling, rollback, and focused tests before implementation.

options.title: Keep Restore User-Driven
options.body: Enhance `backup create` with safer platform-targeted output, conversion, verification, and docs while avoiding automated archive writes into live state.

options.title: Route Most Scope To Plugins
options.body: Keep core to backup verification and plugin/API seams while recommending ClawHub/plugin solutions for sync, cloud backup, and optional restore workflows unless a missing core API is proven.

recommendation.title: Design Minimal Core Migration Contract
recommendation.body: Define a preview-first first-party export/import or backup-restore contract with safe extraction, explicit secret/session policy, path remapping, conflict handling, rollback, and focused tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They have both backup path-safety history and the clearest prior product/security objection to automated restore in the linked implementation discussion.
